name: The Instruction Hierarchy (Privileged Instructions)
executive_summary: Train models to prioritize instructions by source privilege — system over developer over user over third-party content — so lower-privilege text can never override higher-privilege ones.
description: Formalizes instruction privilege as an explicit, trainable, checkable property rather than an implicit assumption: defines a strict ordering of instruction sources (system > developer > user > tool/third-party content) and trains the model to resolve conflicts by source privilege rather than recency or phrasing. The strongest existing academic match for any project's own privilege/authority lattice design.
when_to_use: Designing a system with multiple instruction sources of differing trust levels (system prompt, developer instructions, end-user input, third-party/tool content).
when_not_to_use: Single-source-of-instruction systems with no privilege distinctions to enforce.
known_pitfalls: Privilege modeling still requires the model to correctly attribute which channel a given piece of text came from; misattribution defeats the hierarchy.

primary_source.authors: Wallace, Xiao, Leike, Weng, Heidecke, Beutel
primary_source.title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: This template describes a training-time process (fine-tuning or policy training), not a single reproducible inference call; reproducibility depends on the training pipeline and data, not on prompt text alone.
